title: Do not back away from ideas
summary: Wilson says young improvisers should pursue every idea as Pete Brown, Parker and Bud Freeman did.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: And that's another thing a young person should never do -- when you're developing and improvising, don't back away from any idea. And that's another thing -- Pete Brown was like that on the alto.
He'd get these brainstorms, he may not make them perfectly -- and Charlie Parker, too.
Yes. And Charlie wasn't flawless, like when he died -- in the early days, he wasn't playing that flawlessly.
He went from Cab Calloway to ...
Sure, he'd go for a pattern and couldn't make it and he'd have to wait a long time, and then he'd pick up the thread until finally that stuff started tying together.
That's right -- Cab Calloway used to bawl him out, man.

Oh, what was that tenor player I mentioned -- Bud Freeman, he's playing better now in his 70's than he did when he was in his 30's, because he was playing a very disjointed, incoherent stuttering type of thing, but he's got it all connected. He's flowing now, but the only way you get it to flow is to not back away and play it safe, but improvise -- you got to go for that idea, whether you make it or not. You've got to try to follow that intention and keep it and follow through with it.
Because once you back away from it, your plan is weakened a great deal, don't you think?
